You need to know the model. A German WWII era Mauser is likely a 98. Then your best bet is to keep an eye out on sites such as gunbroker.com, or even eBay. There will also be hardware involved, if you don't currently have it. Barrel bands that fit the stock to the rifle. It's not hard to do, it'll just take finding the right parts, and then returning it to original condition. On Mauser's though, each part is often numbered to match the serial number of the rifle itself. Example ... if the serial number of the rifle is 555367, all the parts may be stamped with the last two or three digits, like 367 or 67. So you won't likely be able to find a numbered matching part. But you could get it to look close to it's former configuration.
